questions.content:
An accounting firm has five senior partners who saw 6, 4, 3, 7, and 5 clients yesterday.

a. Compute the mean and median number of clients.

b. Is the mean a sample mean or a population mean?

c. Verify that $\sum_{i=1}^{5}(x_i-\mu)=0$.
Explain how the population mean, median, and mode compare when the relative-frequency curve is (a) symmetric, (b) skewed left, and (c) skewed right.

A random sample of six client-entertainment expenses, in dollars, is $157,132,109,145,125,139$.

a. Show that $\sum(x_i-\bar{x})^2=\sum x_i^2-n\bar{x}^2$.

b. Calculate $\bar{x}$, $s^2$, and $s$ using both formulas.

c. Assuming an approximately normal population, estimate the intervals containing $68.26\%$, $95.44\%$, and $99.73\%$ of expenses.

d. Is an expense of $190$ unusually high? Explain.

The numbers of items purchased by 30 evening customers are

$$15,8,6,9,9,4,18,10,10,12,12,4,7,8,12,10,10,11,9,13,5,6,11,14,5,6,6,5,13,5.$$

Calculate the mean, median, sample standard deviation, range, first quartile, third quartile, and interquartile range. Using the $1.5\times IQR$ rule, determine whether there are outliers.

The shipping times, in days, for 13 rugs are $31,31,42,39,42,43,34,30,28,36,37,35,40$. Calculate the mean and sample standard deviation. What percentage of the observed times lie within two standard deviations of the mean, and is a 60-day delivery likely under an approximately normal model?

Three stock funds have the following mean yearly returns and standard deviations:

| Fund | Mean | Standard deviation |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | $10.93\%$ | $41.96\%$ |
| 2 | $13.00\%$ | $9.36\%$ |
| 3 | $34.45\%$ | $41.16\%$ |

Assume returns are normally distributed.

a. Find an interval containing about $95.44\%$ of returns for each fund.

b. Compare the funds by mean and variability.

c. Calculate each coefficient of variation and rank relative risk.
A student earned 18 semester hours of A, 36 of B, 7 of C, 3 of D, and 0 of F. Assign grade points 4, 3, 2, 1, and 0, respectively. Calculate the GPA and explain why it is a weighted mean.

Canadian women's life expectancy has mean $73.75$ years and standard deviation $6.5$ years.

a. Using Chebyshev's inequality, find the minimum percentage with life expectancy between 64 and 83.5 years.

b. Find bounds on life expectancy such that at least $90\%$ of the population is included.
The numbers of computer monitors produced over 10 days were $24,31,27,25,35,33,26,40,25,28$. Calculate the mean, median, and mode.

questions.content: Five starting basketball players have mean height 76 inches, median 78 inches, and range 11 inches. If the tallest player is replaced by a substitute who is 2 inches taller, find the new mean, median, and range.

questions.content:
Weekly sales, in dollars, for three salespeople over six weeks are:

| Week | A | B | C |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1774 | 1330 | 1402 |
| 2 | 1808 | 1295 | 1665 |
| 3 | 1890 | 1502 | 1530 |
| 4 | 1932 | 1104 | 1826 |
| 5 | 1855 | 1189 | 1703 |
| 6 | 1726 | 1441 | 1498 |

For each salesperson, report the mean, median, sample standard deviation, range, minimum, and maximum. Compare their performance.

questions.content:
The numbers of tornadoes recorded from 1950 to 1994 in 12 states were $1113,2009,1374,1137,2110,1086,1166,1039,1673,2300,1139,5490$.

a. Calculate the mean and median.

b. Identify the outlier, remove it, and recalculate the mean and median.

c. Which summary changes more, and which is the better summary for these data?

questions.content:
A sample of 400 people reports weekly exercise hours. Use the grouped table below to estimate the mean, sample variance, and sample standard deviation.

| Hours | Frequency | Midpoint |
|---|---:|---:|
| $0$ to less than $3.5$ | 34 | 1.75 |
| $3.5$ to less than $7.0$ | 92 | 5.25 |
| $7.0$ to less than $10.5$ | 55 | 8.75 |
| $10.5$ to less than $14.0$ | 83 | 12.25 |
| $14.0$ to less than $28.0$ | 121 | 21.00 |
| $28.0$ to less than $56.0$ | 15 | 42.00 |
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester2-2014-2015/Assignment-Chapter03/GCNU1003 Sp of Stat_assignment ch3 sem2 2014-2015.docx

questions.content: Let $A,B,C,D,E$ be the five outcomes in a sample space. Suppose $P(A)=0.20$, $P(B)=0.15$, $P(C)=0.30$, and $P(D)=0.20$. Find $P(E)$ and explain.

A brokerage report classifies 15 aerospace companies and 25 food retailers by stock risk.

| Company type | Low risk | Moderate-to-high risk | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Aerospace | 6 | 9 | 15 |
| Food retailer | 15 | 10 | 25 |

For a randomly selected company, find: (a) $P(\text{moderate-to-high risk}\mid\text{aerospace})$, (b) the analogous probability given food retailer, and (c) whether company type and risk level are independent.

Of 10,000 college students, 2,500 have a Mastercard, 4,000 have a VISA, and 1,000 have both. Find: (a) $P(V\mid M)$, (b) $P(M\mid V)$, and (c) whether having a Mastercard and having a VISA are independent.

Two patrons independently choose one of three diet colas, A, B, or C.

a. List the nine ordered outcomes.

b. List the outcomes for: (1) both choose A, (2) the same cola, (3) different colas, (4) at least one chooses A, and (5) neither chooses C.

c. Assuming the nine outcomes are equally likely, find the probability of each event.

John watches a television show with probability $0.4$. Jane watches it with probability $0.5$. The conditional probability that John watches it given that Jane does is $0.7$. Find: (a) the probability both watch, (b) $P(\text{Jane}\mid\text{John})$, and (c) whether their viewing is independent.

A cola distributor claims that 80% of people prefer A and 10% prefer each of B and C. Two participants make independent choices.

a. Find the probability of every ordered pair of choices.

b. Find the probability that neither participant chooses A.

c. If neither participant chooses A, explain what this says about the claim.

A random variable $X$ takes values $1,2,3,4,5$ with $p(x)=x/15$.

a. Construct the probability table.

b. Verify the distribution conditions.

c. Calculate $\mu_X$, $\sigma_X^2$, and $\sigma_X$.

Thirty percent of customers make a purchase. Six customers enter independently. Let $X$ be the number who purchase.

a. Write the binomial probability formula.

b. Find $P(X=5)$, $P(X\ge3)$, $P(X\le2)$, and $P(X\ge1)$.

Accidents follow a Poisson process with an average of 1.5 accidents per three months. Find: (a) the probability of no accidents in the next three months, (b) the probability of fewer than four accidents in the next three months, (c) the probability of no more than 12 accidents in a year, and (d) the probability of no accidents in a year.
Raw exam scores are normally distributed. A score of 63 has z-score $-1$, and a score of 93 has z-score $1.5$. Find the mean and standard deviation of raw scores.
Annual health-care expenses for a family of four are normally distributed with mean $3000$ dollars and standard deviation $500$ dollars. What expense cutoff includes the lowest $33\%$ of families?

In a survey of 250 consumers, 40 said they would never shop at a store again after a false electronic-article-surveillance alarm. A company claims that no more than 5% of consumers would say this.

a. Assuming $p=0.05$, use a normal approximation with continuity correction to estimate $P(X\ge40)$.

b. What does this probability suggest about the company's claim?
The numbers of commuter students in four semesters were $8,17,14,17$. Find the mean and median.

questions.content:
The numbers of resident students in four semesters were $22,13,16,13$.

a. Find the mean and median.

b. To compare the total numbers of commuter and resident students across the four semesters, should you compare the means or the medians? Explain why. The commuter-student counts were $8,17,14,17$.
